summary: As of 27 Oct 2026, Behold's free JSON feed is the best fit for an auto-updating grid styled to match the Layers site. It gives up to 6 posts, refreshes once a day, carries no branding in JSON, has CORS `*`, and Behold refreshes the token itself. The catch is that every request to the feed URL counts against 1,200 views a month, and a free account is paused when it hits the limit. So browsers should never call the feed directly. Fetch it through a cached Cloudflare Pages Function, built like the existing `functions/api/menu.js`, and fall back to a hand-picked JSON list. Instagram's own per-post embeds still work. Since 15 Jun 2026 the oEmbed API also works without a token or App Review (tested live). But embeds can't be styled, are not a feed, and are heavy: each post is an iframe of about 500 KB of HTML plus a dozen scripts. The iframe also sets `csrftoken` and `mid` cookies on `.instagram.com` (about 400 days, SameSite=None). Fetching from Meta yourself needs a Business or Creator account, a Business-type Meta app, Standard Access (no App Review for your own account) and a 60-day token that must be refreshed before it expires; an expired token cannot be refreshed. That is ongoing upkeep the client can't do. Among other widgets, SnapWidget and LightWidget have unlimited free views but are iframes with no JSON. Elfsight (200 views), Juicer (300), EmbedSocial (500) and Curator (2,000) have view caps, and Elfsight and Juicer show their branding (likely Curator too). On free tiers, only Behold gives JSON. Every service requires a Business or Creator account, except Elfsight, which can read a public personal account.

findings.detail: Free $0/mo: '1,200 views / mo', '1 source, 1 feed', '6 max posts per feed', 'Updates once a day', 'Limited widget styles', 'Behold logo on hover' (applies to the widget; JSON has no visible branding, since you render it), 'JSON feeds' included. A free account is paused when it hits the view limit, until the next month. Paid plans: Starter $10 (15k views, 3 feeds, 50 posts, hourly, no logo); Pro $30 (125k views, every 5 min); Business $60; Scale $180. Paid plans are paused only if the limit is exceeded two months in a row.

findings.topic: Behold view counting for JSON feeds
findings.detail: FAQ: 'For JSON feeds, a view is counted every time a request hits our servers for a feed URL.' 'Media requests (images and videos) are not counted.' Behold emails you when the monthly limit is hit. So if each visitor's browser fetches the feed directly, the 1,200 free views run out fast. A server-side cache in front of the feed is required on the free plan.

findings.topic: Behold JSON feed URL and response shape
findings.detail: The URL is https://feeds.behold.so/<feed-id>, and a GET returns a JSON object. Top-level fields: username, biography, profilePictureUrl, website, followersCount, followsCount, posts[] (hashtag feeds also have hashtags[]). Each post has id, timestamp (ISO 8601), permalink, mediaType (IMAGE | VIDEO | CAROUSEL_ALBUM), isReel (VIDEO only), mediaUrl (raw Instagram original, very large; for VIDEO it is the video file), thumbnailUrl (VIDEO only), sizes {small, medium, large, full}, each {mediaUrl, width, height}, caption, prunedCaption (hashtags removed, trailing separators and whitespace cleaned), altText (not available for Reels or hashtag feeds), hashtags[], mentions[], likeCount, commentsCount, colorPalette {dominant, muted, mutedLight, mutedDark, vibrant, vibrantLight, vibrantDark} as 'R,G,B' strings, and children[] (CAROUSEL_ALBUM only). The @behold/types npm package has TypeScript types. Feed settings: number of posts, allowed post types, caption must or must not include (case-sensitive), off-feed reels, and a domain whitelist. The docs say the whitelist is not a strong security measure, and localhost is always allowed.

findings.topic: Behold sizes and the v2 shape
findings.detail: In v2, feeds return an object with posts[] (v1 basic feeds returned a bare array). `dimensions` was removed and `sizes` added: optimized WebP at max 400/700/1000/2000 px, aspect ratio kept. For VIDEO posts, `sizes` holds a thumbnail and the video stays at mediaUrl. Use `sizes`, not mediaUrl, in production.

Live GET of the docs' example feed on 2026-10-27 returned `access-control-allow-origin: *`, `access-control-allow-methods: GET,HEAD`, `cache-control: public, max-age=10, s-maxage=10`, served via Cloudflare. Image URLs in `sizes` were on https://behold.pictures/<token>.jpg?class=originalSmall|Medium|Large|Full and came back as `content-type: image/webp` with ACAO `*` and `cache-control: public, max-age=2592000` (30 days). Real response keys matched the docs, plus an undocumented `visibility` field. altText was missing on 5 of the 6 sample posts. timestamp looks like '2020-09-04T22:26:14+0000'. Browser fetch works, but every fetch costs a view.

findings.topic: Behold account type, authorization and token upkeep
findings.detail: 'Only Business or Media Creator Instagram accounts can be connected to Behold.' A personal account would need switching to professional, which is free. Someone without login access can copy an 'auth link', and the account owner (e.g. the social media manager) authorizes it without logging in to Behold. All permissions must be granted, including the ones marked optional. The JSON-feeds page says Behold handles creating and refreshing access tokens. The only manual upkeep: 'If the password or privacy of a connected Instagram account is changed you will have to reauthorize the source', by reopening the same auth link. A basic source has no periodic re-auth. An advanced source (Facebook User method) needs re-auth every 3 months; it is only needed for hashtag feeds.

FAQ: 'We care about privacy, and do not collect or store any of your visitor's personal data.' The widget embed is <behold-widget feed-id="..."></behold-widget> plus a module loader script from https://w.behold.so/widget.js. It is styled from Behold's dashboard ('Customize', 'Gallery wall design', per-breakpoint post count). It is less flexible than rendering the JSON yourself, and on the free plan it shows the Behold logo on hover.

Meta's blog says that on June 15, 2026 the access-token requirement was lifted from all Meta oEmbed APIs (Instagram, Threads, FB Post, FB Video), and App Review ('Meta oEmbed Read') is no longer needed for public content. Token-based access still works. 'Rate limits may differ' for tokenless calls. Response: version, provider_name, provider_url, html, width, type. Confirmed live: an unauthenticated GET https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/instagram_oembed?url=https://www.instagram.com/p/<code>/ returned 200 with the blockquote HTML plus <script async src="//platform.instagram.com/en_US/embeds.js">.

Endpoint: GET graph.facebook.com/{version}/instagram_oembed. Parameters: url (/p/, /reel/, /{username}), maxwidth (320-658; maxheight not supported), omitscript (load embed.js yourself, then call instgrm.Embeds.process()), hidecaption, fields. Not supported: private, inactive or age-restricted accounts, accounts that have disabled embeds, Stories, and Shadow DOM. Use is restricted to front-end display ('any purpose other than providing a front-end view ... is strictly prohibited'), so you cannot scrape the oEmbed HTML to build a custom-styled grid. The rate limit on the page is 1,000 requests per hour.

findings.topic: oEmbed thumbnail and author fields removed
findings.detail: Search results summarizing Meta's changelog say author_name, author_url, thumbnail_url, thumbnail_width and thumbnail_height were deprecated, with full removal on Nov 3, 2025. A live response had none of these fields, which matches. So oEmbed cannot supply grid thumbnails.

findings.topic: Weight and privacy of Instagram blockquote embeds
findings.detail: Measured live: https://www.instagram.com/embed.js (platform.instagram.com/en_US/embeds.js 301-redirects to it) is 65,133 bytes (about 21.9 KB gzipped), cache max-age 1200. embed.js swaps each blockquote for an iframe. That iframe's document (/p/<code>/embed/captioned/) was about 506 KB of HTML with 72 script tags (12+ external JS bundles from static.cdninstagram.com). It set `csrftoken` and `mid` cookies on .instagram.com (Max-Age 34,560,000 s, about 400 days, SameSite=None; mid is httponly). These are third-party cookies on every visit, and the cost repeats per embedded post. The embed is a fixed Instagram white card (min-width 326px, max 658px) that can't be restyled. It is not a feed: each post is pasted by hand.

Meta announced the Instagram Basic Display API deprecation on Sep 4, 2024, and from Dec 4, 2024 all requests return errors. Personal-account feeds via the API ended then; the replacement needs a professional (Business or Creator) account. Primary-page wording was not re-read; this comes from Meta's docs as summarized in search results and from vendor notices.

findings.topic: Self-hosted: Instagram API with Instagram Login
findings.detail: Requires an Instagram professional account (business or creator); no Facebook Page needed. Host is graph.instagram.com. Scope is instagram_business_basic (replaced business_basic on Jan 27, 2025). Create a new app of type Business if your current one isn't. Standard Access is enough for accounts you own or manage and have added to the app; Advanced Access (App Review plus Business Verification) is only needed to serve accounts you don't manage. In the App Dashboard, 'API setup with Instagram business login', click 'Generate token' to get a long-lived token valid for 60 days; tokens from the login flow last 1 hour. Exchange a short-lived token with GET https://graph.instagram.com/access_token?grant_type=ig_exchange_token&client_secret=...&access_token=... (server side only). Refresh with GET https://graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token?grant_type=ig_refresh_token&access_token=...; the token must be at least 24 h old and unexpired, and the refreshed one is valid 60 days. 'Tokens that have not been refreshed in 60 days will expire and can no longer be refreshed.' Media: GET /<IG_ID>/media (or /me with fields=user_id,username); fields include id, caption, media_type, media_url, permalink, thumbnail_url (VIDEO), timestamp, alt_text, children edge. media_url can be omitted for videos with copyrighted audio, so fall back to thumbnail_url or permalink. The edge returns at most the 10K newest media, and Stories are not included.

findings.topic: Instagram Platform overview (access levels, Unified Login)
findings.detail: App users 'must have an Instagram professional account'. 'Standard Access is all your app needs' if you only serve accounts you own or manage. Advanced Access 'requires App Review and Business Verification'. Long-lived tokens last 60 days and can be refreshed. A newer 'Instagram API with Unified Login' is marked recommended for new integrations. It needs a Business portfolio, uses a 'Business Integration System User Access Token' on graph.facebook.com, and the page does not say whether that token expires. The rolling rate limit is 4800 × impressions per 24 h.

findings.topic: Cloudflare Cache API scope (affects Behold quota math)
findings.detail: The Cache API is per data center: cached content 'do[es] not replicate outside of the originating data center'. Pages Functions get cache access on custom domains and *.pages.dev. put() respects Cache-Control; stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error are not supported with put or match. Implication: Behold sees about one request per TTL per Cloudflare colo, so keep the TTL at 12 h or more on the free plan. Cron Triggers are documented for Workers, not Pages Functions; scheduled work would need a separate Worker or a deploy hook.

Free: as many widgets as you like, 'no view limit', refreshes every 15 minutes, one account per free widget, Instagram or Facebook. Clicking a photo 'opens a SnapWidget page', which sends visitors off-site. Requires a Creator or Business account, because 'Meta does not let apps connect to personal accounts'. Paid: Lite $8/mo, Pro $14/mo, Developer $99/mo. No JSON or API is mentioned. Per SnapWidget's own embed page (seen in search results), the embed is an iframe plus their script and CSS.

Free: $0, views unlimited, no watermark or ads, content refreshes every 24 h (30 min on paid), no CDN, JPEG only (no WebP or AVIF), no 'expired token notifications' (paid only). Editing settings means changing the embed code. Upgrade costs $15 one-time per widget, and image optimization $39/yr. Requires a professional account (Business or Creator), via Instagram Login or Facebook Login. Tokens 'have an expiration date and may require renewal', with manual 'Refresh token' in the dashboard. No JSON. The embed is iframe-based (the site says it works where iframes are supported).

Free: 200 views/month ('Exceeding this monthly limit will temporarily deactivate your app'), 1 widget, Elfsight branding. Paid tiers are '100% Ad Free', from $5/mo billed yearly. FAQ: 'You can use a public personal account without login', with automatic refresh every 48 hours. No JSON. Embed is a platform.js script plus a div with data-elfsight-app-lazy; That syntax comes from Elfsight help and community search results, not the pricing page.

Free: 1 feed, 1 source or hashtag, refresh every 24 h, 300 feed views/month, Juicer branding (removed from Lite $15/mo, $13.50 yearly). Social-wall API access is listed only on Enterprise (from $199/mo). There is a separate developer API at api.juicer.io/v1 with Bearer keys and a free Sandbox of 30 one-time credits. No JSON on free.

'The Free plan is permanent, with 1 source, 500 views a month, and 500 media per source', unlimited widgets, refresh every 24 h. The cheapest paid plan is Pro at $29/mo. The EmbedSocial API is on Premium ($99/mo) and Enterprise only. Branding and whether Instagram is in the Free column could not be read from the page.

Free $0: 3 sources, 1,000 posts max, 2,000 views/month, refresh every 24 h. 'No Powered by Curator link' is listed as a Pro and Business benefit, which implies the free plan shows the link. Pro is about $23-25/mo, Business about $54-59/mo. API access is Business only, and the docs say the API key must not be used in client-side code.

findings.topic: Pages CMS for the no-account fallback
findings.detail: Pages CMS is free and MIT-licensed, edits content and media directly in a GitHub repo, and currently supports GitHub only. Config file: .pages.yml at the repo root. It supports media: {input, output}, and content entries with type: file, path, format (json, yaml, ...), list, and fields; image fields use type: image. A non-technical manager can upload a photo plus paste a post link, and the edit commits to the repo, which triggers the Cloudflare Pages build.

The Layers site runs on Cloudflare Pages with Pages Functions; functions/api/menu.js already does edge-cached, fallback-first JSON (caches.default, s-maxage TTL, last-known-good fallback). Pages are built by tools/build-pages.py into public/. CSS already has an .sr-only utility, and there is no CSP or _headers file yet. An /api/instagram function built the same way fits the existing code.

gotchas: Never fetch https://feeds.behold.so/<id> straight from visitors' browsers on the free plan. Every request counts as a view (1,200 a month), and a free account is paused until the next month when it hits the cap. Put the cached Pages Function in front.

Cloudflare's Cache API is per data center, so Behold sees about one request per TTL per colo, not one in total. Keep IG_TTL at 12 h or more: 2 requests/day × 30 days × a handful of colos stays well under 1,200. The free feed only updates once a day anyway.

With Behold free, a new Instagram post can take up to 24 h, plus your cache TTL, to appear on the site. Tell the social media manager this up front. Starter ($10/mo) updates hourly and removes the view-pause risk.

Behold, SnapWidget, LightWidget and the Meta API all require a Business or Creator account; only Elfsight claims public personal accounts work. Check that @layerssuperfoodbar is professional (switching is free and keeps posts). Create the Behold account under the client's email, and have the manager authorize through Behold's auth link.

If the Instagram password or privacy setting changes, the Behold source must be reauthorized via the same auth link. Leave a one-line note in the handoff doc. What Behold serves after an auth break (stale posts vs an error) is undocumented, so the function treats non-2xx or fewer than 3 posts as failure and serves the fallback.

Behold's domain whitelist filters by request origin. A server-side fetch from the Pages Function has no browser Origin, so test before turning the whitelist on, or leave it blank. The docs call it not a strong security measure.

Use posts[].sizes.* (optimized WebP on behold.pictures, 30-day cache), not mediaUrl. mediaUrl is the huge raw Instagram original, and for VIDEO it is the video file; for videos and reels, sizes holds the thumbnail.

altText is often missing (missing on 5 of 6 sample posts, never on Reels or hashtag feeds). Fall back to the first prunedCaption line or a generic description, and ask the manager to fill in Instagram's 'Write alt text' setting.

Captions are user content (emoji, URLs, @mentions). Always set them through textContent or attributes, never innerHTML. Validate permalink hosts (instagram.com) and image hosts (behold.pictures or same origin) before rendering.

Behold timestamps look like '2020-09-04T22:26:14+0000' (no colon in the offset). If you show dates, normalize with .replace(/([+-]\d{2})(\d{2})$/, '$1:$2') before new Date(); older Safari parses this format inconsistently. Not tested.

Instagram's own embeds carry third-party cookies: the iframe sets csrftoken and mid on .instagram.com, about 400 days, SameSite=None. Each one is about 500 KB of HTML plus a dozen scripts per post, fixed white card styling (326-658px), and a manual per-post paste. They also fail if the account has turned off 'allow embeds', and oEmbed HTML may only be used for front-end display, not scraped into a custom grid.
Tokenless oEmbed (since 15 Jun 2026) may have lower rate limits than token-based access. thumbnail_url and author_name were removed (Nov 2025), so oEmbed can't power a thumbnail grid.

Self-hosting the Meta API means a 60-day token that must be refreshed while still valid (at least 24 h old); 'Tokens that have not been refreshed in 60 days will expire and can no longer be refreshed.' Pages Functions have no cron, so you'd need a separate Worker cron plus KV. Instagram media_url values are CDN links that seem to expire (inferred), so you'd also have to re-host images. That breaks the zero-maintenance requirement.

SnapWidget free sends clicks to a SnapWidget page (off-site), and LightWidget free has no expired-token alerts. Elfsight free deactivates after 200 views a month and shows its branding; Juicer free gives 300 views with branding; EmbedSocial 500 views; Curator 2,000 views and likely a 'Powered by Curator' link. None of them offers JSON on the free tier.

If a CSP is added later (none exists now), allow img-src https://behold.pictures https://*.behold.pictures. The live feed uses behold.pictures, while the v2 docs show cdn.behold.pictures and cdn2.behold.pictures.

On the list, use role="list" with list-style:none, or Safari/VoiceOver drops list semantics. Give images width and height to avoid layout shift, and only animate hover zoom under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

Pages CMS only works with GitHub repos. Its commits only change the live site if Cloudflare Pages builds from that repo. The README says public/ is deployed as-is, so either point the CMS at public/ (as in the snippet) or have the CF build run tools/build-pages.py. Per the project rule, deploy only after Meni's OK.
recommendation:
(a) Auto-updating grid styled to the site: use a Behold free JSON feed on a basic source (Business or Creator account, authorized by the social media manager through Behold's auth link, with Behold handling token refresh). Proxy it through a new Cloudflare Pages Function `/api/instagram` that copies the existing `menu.js` pattern: about 12 h edge cache, URL validation, and a short-cached fallback on any error or pause. Render 6 square tiles with the site's own CSS tokens, lazy WebP `srcset` from `sizes`, `colorPalette.dominant` as the placeholder colour, sr-only "(on Instagram)" link text, and Video/Reel/Album badges. The section pre-renders the hand-picked fallback in HTML, so no-JS visitors, timeouts, Behold outages or a paused feed degrade cleanly. Visitors' browsers then contact only the site and behold.pictures for images (Behold says it stores no visitor data). Cost $0 and no upkeep beyond reauthorizing after a password change. If posts must appear within the hour, or traffic grows, move to Behold Starter ($10/mo). Do not use Instagram's per-post embeds for the grid, because of the third-party cookies, about 500 KB per post, no styling and manual pasting. Do not self-host the Meta API, because of the 60-day token chores. Rule out the iframe widget services: no JSON, view caps or branding, and SnapWidget sends clicks off-site.

(b) No-account fallback: keep 6 hand-picked posts in `public/assets/data/instagram-fallback.json`, holding the photo path, post link and alt text. The social media manager edits it through a free Pages CMS form (`.pages.yml` above): upload a photo, paste the post link, describe the photo. Saving commits to GitHub and the Pages build updates the site. The same JSON drives the static pre-render and the function's fallback. Leaving `BEHOLD_FEED_ID` unset makes the whole section run in this mode with no code change. Add a "Follow @layerssuperfoodbar" link under the grid in both modes.

summary:
Every topic was checked against primary sources on Oct 27 2026: GitHub Docs, the actions/* release pages and READMEs, the gh manual, Pages CMS docs, Cloudflare Pages and Web Analytics docs, and the wrangler-action repo.

**Current major versions (from release pages; the pages show day and month but no year, so 2026 is inferred):**
- actions/checkout@v7
- actions/setup-python@v7
- actions/cache@v6
- actions/configure-pages@v6
- actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
- actions/deploy-pages@v5
- actions/upload-artifact@v7
- actions/download-artifact@v8
- cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4

GitHub's own Pages docs examples still show older tags (configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v4, deploy-pages@v4).

**GitHub Pages and triggers:**
- The deploy job needs `pages: write` and `id-token: write`.
- On GitHub Free the repo must be public. GitHub Pro (free through the Student Developer Pack) can serve Pages from a private repo, but the site is still public.
- To switch the source to Actions: PUT (or POST to create) `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` with `build_type=workflow`.
- Pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not start new workflow runs, except `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch`.
- GitHub tells you to use a GitHub App installation token or a personal access token when you need runs to trigger. So Pages CMS commits (made with its app installation token or the user's OAuth token) do trigger `on: push`.

**Schedules:** cron runs in UTC by default, and a new optional `timezone:` key is documented. The minimum interval is 5 minutes. Schedules run only on the default branch. The 60-day auto-disable is documented for public repos only.

**Backups:**
- Release assets: each file under 2 GiB, up to 1000 per release, no limit on total size or bandwidth.
- Releases need `contents: write`.
- Artifact retention is 1–90 days (public) or 1–400 days (private), default 90.

**Cloudflare Pages:**
- Build images v1/v2/v3. Default Python is 3.13.3 on v3 and 3.11.5 on v2. v1 projects were auto-moved to v3 on Sep 15 2026; v2 moves on Feb 23 2027.
- Whether requirements.txt is installed automatically is not documented. The docs only mention automatic installs with a `SKIP_DEPENDENCY_INSTALL` opt-out, and pip is not in the build cache.
- Limits: 20-minute builds, 500 builds/month on Free, 20,000 files (Free), 25 MiB per file.
- `wrangler pages deploy` uploads a `functions/` folder found in the directory it runs from.
- A Direct Upload project can never be switched to Git integration.
- Rollback: Deployments > All deployments > ⋯ > "Rollback to this deployment" (only successful production deployments).

**Web Analytics:** free, no cookies or localStorage. Sites not proxied by Cloudflare use the beacon script with a token, with a soft limit of 10 such sites. Pages projects have an Enable toggle under Metrics that injects the snippet on the next deployment.

**Instagram widgets:** the relayed request also mentioned Instagram widgets. This brief didn't cover them and their embed requirements weren't researched. The only overlap is that the site's CSP (`_headers`) would have to allow whatever an embed loads.

findings.detail: Latest major is v7 (v7.0.1 marked Latest; v7.0.0 released 18 Jun, and the linked changelog is dated 2026-06-18). The README uses actions/checkout@v7. v7 blocks fork-PR checkout under pull_request_target/workflow_run unless `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` is set, and moved the code to ESM. In v6, persist-credentials writes credentials to a file under $RUNNER_TEMP instead of .git/config. v5 moved to Node 24 and needs runner v2.327.1 or later.

Latest major is v7 (v7.1.0 marked Latest, dated 22 Oct). The README example is `uses: actions/setup-python@v7` with `python-version: '3.13'` and `cache: 'pip'`. `cache-dependency-path` controls which file is hashed for the cache key. v6 moved to node24 and needs runner v2.327.1 or later.

Latest major is v6 (v6.1.0). v5 moved to Node 24; v4 moved to the cache service v2 APIs. Limits: 10 GB of caches per repo, least-recently-accessed eviction, and caches unused for 7 days are evicted. Cache storage is separate from artifacts/Packages, with 10 GB included per repo. You don't need it directly when using setup-python's `cache: pip`.

configure-pages: v6.0.0 is Latest (Node 24; runs.using node24). Its `enablement` input defaults to 'false', and enabling it needs a token other than GITHUB_TOKEN. Outputs are base_url, origin, host, base_path. upload-pages-artifact: v5.0.0 is Latest (moves to upload-artifact v7 and adds an `include-hidden-files` input). Since v4, dotfiles are excluded by default. Inputs are path (default `_site/`), name (default `github-pages`), retention-days (default 1). deploy-pages: v5.0.1 is Latest (v5.0.0 moved to Node 24.x). The actions/starter-workflows pages/static.yml already uses deploy-pages@v5. GitHub's 'Using custom workflows' doc still shows configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v4, deploy-pages@v4, checkout@v6.

upload-artifact: latest major v7 (v7.0.2, 7 Oct). v7 adds `archive: false` for single-file uploads; v6 defaults to Node 24. retention-days minimum is 1, maximum 90 unless changed in repo settings. `include-hidden-files` and `overwrite` default to false; compression-level 0–9, default 6. Limit of 500 artifacts per job, and v4+ artifacts are immutable. download-artifact: latest major v8 (v8.0.2).

From the docs: "The job must have a minimum of `pages: write` and `id-token: write` permissions." The default environment is `github-pages`; it is auto-created and should be protected to the default branch. Use the `page_url` output for environment.url. The starter workflow uses `concurrency: group: "pages", cancel-in-progress: false`.

Published site no larger than 1 GB. Recommended source repo limit 1 GB. Deployments time out after 10 minutes. Soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB/month. The soft limit of 10 builds/hour does NOT apply to custom GitHub Actions workflows. Rate-limited requests get HTTP 429. upload-pages-artifact's README says 10 GB is an unofficial hard limit.

findings.topic: GitHub Pages from a private repo (Free vs Pro/Student)
findings.detail: From the docs: "If the account that owns the repository uses GitHub Free or GitHub Free for organizations, the repository must be public." The plans page lists GitHub Pages for Pro under private-repo features. Publishing a site privately (access-controlled) needs an organization on Enterprise Cloud. Sites are "publicly available on the internet, even if the repository for the site is private." The Student Developer Pack lists "Free GitHub Pro while you are a student."

findings.topic: Switch Pages source to GitHub Actions via REST
findings.detail: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages creates a site (body `build_type`: "legacy" | "workflow", optional `source`); returns 201. PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages updates it (`build_type`, `cname`, `https_enforced`, `source`); returns 204. The caller must be a repo admin/maintainer or have 'manage GitHub Pages settings'. Classic PATs need `repo`. The fine-grained permission table lists PUT under both Pages (write) and Administration (write). In the UI: Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source = GitHub Actions.

findings.topic: GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not trigger workflows
findings.detail: From the docs: "events triggered by the `GITHUB_TOKEN` will not create a new workflow run, with the following exceptions: `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` events always create workflow runs." Also: "if a workflow run pushes code using the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a new workflow will not run even when the repository contains a workflow configured to run when `push` events occur." The docs suggest using "a GitHub App installation access token or a personal access token instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN`".

findings.topic: Pages CMS commits (App installation token) trigger on: push
findings.detail: Pages CMS writes with the signed-in user's GitHub token when it has access. Otherwise it uses the repo's GitHub App installation token (collaborator fallback). With the app token, commits are attributed to the app by default (`settings.commit.identity: app`); `identity: user` sends the user's name/email as committer. Neither is GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub tells you to use exactly these tokens when you need runs to trigger, so Pages CMS commits fire `on: push`. That last step is an inference: GitHub doesn't state 'installation-token pushes trigger push' in those words, but its suppression rule is scoped to GITHUB_TOKEN only. The Pages CMS app requests Actions read/write and subscribes to Push and Workflow run webhooks. Default commit message template is "Update {path} (via Pages CMS)".

POSIX cron with 5 fields. "By default, scheduled workflows run in UTC." An optional IANA `timezone:` key sits next to `cron:` (e.g. `- cron: '30 5 * * 1-5'` with `timezone: "America/New_York"`). The shortest interval is every 5 minutes. Runs can be delayed under high load, which includes the start of every hour. Scheduled workflows run only on the default branch. "In a public repository, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled when no repository activity has occurred in 60 days". The docs scope this to public repos and say nothing about private ones. Re-enable from the Actions tab or with `gh workflow enable WORKFLOW`.

"Secrets cannot be directly referenced in `if:` conditionals." The documented workaround is to set secrets as job-level env vars and test `env.X` in step `if:`. In the context availability table, jobs.<id>.if allows github, needs, vars, inputs; steps.if allows env (not secrets); jobs.<id>.env allows secrets.

"Each file included in a release must be under 2 GiB. There is no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage." Up to 1000 assets per release. `gh release create [<tag>] [<filename>...]` takes --title, --notes/-F, --target (branch or full SHA), --latest=false, --draft, --verify-tag. A missing tag is created from the default branch, or from --target. `gh release list` takes -L (default 30), --json createdAt,isDraft,isImmutable,isLatest,isPrerelease,name,publishedAt,tagName, --jq, --order. `gh release delete <tag> --cleanup-tag --yes`. `gh release download [<tag>] --pattern --dir --clobber`. In Actions, gh needs `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`. POST/DELETE releases and DELETE git refs need Contents: write.

With immutable releases enabled, a release's assets and tag can't be changed after publication. You can delete an immutable release and its tag, but "you cannot reuse the same tag name". The guidance is to create as draft, attach all assets, then publish. Use unique timestamped tags so pruning never collides.

Default retention 90 days. Configurable 1–90 days in public repos and 1–400 days in private repos. Actions is free on public repos with standard runners. Private repos include 500 MB artifact storage on Free and 1 GB on Pro (2,000 and 3,000 minutes respectively). Artifacts expire, so they are weaker than Releases for long-term backups.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the GITHUB_TOKEN no-trigger rule. POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{workflow_id}/dispatches needs Actions: write (fine-grained table), takes at most 25 inputs, and returns 200 with workflow_run_id/run_url/html_url. Input `type` must be one of boolean, choice, number, environment, string.

Images v1/v2/v3. v3 defaults: Python 3.13.3, pip 26.2.2, Poetry 2.1.3, pipx 1.7.1. v2 Python is 3.11.5. Base is Ubuntu 22.04.2 x86_64. Set the version with `PYTHON_VERSION` or a `.python-version` / `runtime.txt` file. v3 does not support pipenv/Pipfile. v1 projects were auto-moved to v3 on September 15, 2026; v2 projects move on February 23, 2027. Dependencies are installed automatically unless `SKIP_DEPENDENCY_INSTALL=1|true`, but no page says requirements.txt is auto-installed. Build caching (v2+) covers npm/yarn/pnpm/bun only, not pip.

Not documented. The build-image, language-support, build-configuration and MkDocs pages never say requirements.txt is installed. To be safe, put `pip install -r requirements.txt && python build.py` in the Pages build command if you use Git integration.

500 builds/month on Free. "Builds will timeout after 20 minutes." 1 concurrent build on Free. "up to 20,000 files on the Free plan". Paid plans allow 100,000 files, which requires `PAGES_WRANGLER_MAJOR_VERSION=4`. "The maximum file size for a single Cloudflare Pages site asset is 25 MiB." 100 custom domains per project on Free and 100 projects per account. `_headers`: 100 rules, 2,000 chars per header. `_redirects`: 2,000 static + 100 dynamic. Functions requests count toward the Workers plan quota (100,000 daily requests shared with Workers on Free, reset at midnight UTC). Static asset requests are free and unlimited.

findings.topic: Cloudflare Pages Functions with wrangler pages deploy
findings.detail: "Make sure that the `/functions` directory is at the root of your Pages project (and not in the static root, such as `/dist`)." With Wrangler, a `functions` folder in the directory you run the command from is uploaded with the project. Dashboard drag-and-drop does not support Functions. Limits are 20,000 files and 25 MiB via Wrangler, 1,000 files via drag-and-drop. `_routes.json` is auto-generated when a functions dir is detected (max 100 include/exclude rules, 100 chars each). Routing: `functions/api/x.js` maps to `/api/x`; `[param].js` matches one segment, `[[param]].js` matches any depth.

findings.topic: Direct Upload vs Git integration lock-in
findings.detail: Once you choose Direct Upload, the project can't be moved to Git integration; you'd have to create a new project. Create one with `npx wrangler pages project create <NAME> --production-branch=main`. Deploy with `npx wrangler pages deploy <DIR> [--project-name] [--branch] [--commit-hash] [--commit-message] [--commit-dirty]`.

Latest major is v4 (v4.1.3 Latest). v4.1.0 and v4.1.1 are marked broken ("will fail when used in a workflow"), so use @v4 or v4.1.2+. v4 installs Wrangler v4 by default; pin with `wranglerVersion`. Inputs: apiToken, accountId, command, workingDirectory, wranglerVersion, gitHubToken (enables GitHub Deployments), packageManager. Outputs: deployment-url, pages-deployment-alias-url, command-output, command-stderr. Cloudflare's CI doc: permissions `contents: read`, `deployments: write`; API token permission Account > Cloudflare Pages > Edit; secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.

Dashboard: project > Deployments > All deployments > three-dot menu > "Rollback to this deployment" > confirm, and production switches instantly. "Any production deployment that has been successfully built is a valid rollback target"; preview deployments are not. You can roll forward to newer deployments afterwards. There is also an API endpoint: POST /accounts/{account_id}/pages/projects/{project_name}/deployments/{deployment_id}/rollback. This endpoint appears only in search results from the API reference and did not open that page.

"Privacy-first, lightweight, accurate web analytics—for free"; "does not use any client-side state, such as cookies or localStorage"; no fingerprinting. Non-proxied site: Web Analytics > Add a site > hostname > copy the JS snippet and paste it before </body>. Token attribute: `data-cf-beacon='{"token": "$SITE_TOKEN"}'`; tag-manager form: `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js?token=$SITE_TOKEN`. Pages project: Workers & Pages > project > Metrics > Web Analytics > Enable, and the snippet is added automatically on the next deployment. Soft limit of 10 non-proxied sites, no limit for proxied. CSP: script-src https://static.cloudflareinsights.com; connect-src cloudflareinsights.com (manual) or 'self' (auto-injection). Ad blockers can block the beacon. Unsampled data is kept 7 days, then aggregated; 6 months are viewable. Breaks if the origin sends `Cache-Control: public, no-transform` (proxied auto-inject).

findings.topic: Pages toggle on a Direct Upload project
findings.detail: The docs describe the Metrics > Web Analytics Enable toggle for Pages projects without separating Git vs Direct Upload projects. It isn't confirmed to work on a wrangler-deployed project.

config_snippets:
# =====================================================================
# 0) One-time setup commands
# =====================================================================
# Switch GitHub Pages source to "GitHub Actions" (needs repo admin):
#   first time (no Pages site yet):
gh api -X POST repos/OWNER/REPO/pages -f build_type=workflow
#   existing branch-based site -> Actions:
gh api -X PUT  repos/OWNER/REPO/pages -f build_type=workflow
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pages --jq .build_type        # -> "workflow"

# Create the Cloudflare Pages project as Direct Upload (cannot switch to Git integration later!)
npx wrangler pages project create my-site --production-branch=main
# Repo secrets: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (Account > Cloudflare Pages > Edit), CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
# Repo variable: CF_PAGES_PROJECT=my-site   (vars.* IS allowed in job-level if:)

# =====================================================================
# 1) .github/workflows/site.yml  - build+validate on push/PR (pip cache),
#    deploy to GitHub Pages, optional Cloudflare deploy gated on secrets
# =====================================================================
name: Build & deploy site
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]          # Pages CMS commits (App/user token) DO trigger this
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:          # also lets restore.yml kick a rebuild via GITHUB_TOKEN

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:              # Pages CMS = 1 commit per save -> collapse bursts
      group: build-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'           # matches CF build image v3 default (3.13.3)
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements.txt
      - run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt   # Pillow numpy opencv-python-headless pillow-heif jinja2
      - name: Build
        run: python build.py                # writes public/
      - name: Validate output against CF Pages + GH Pages limits
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import os, sys
          root = "public"
          if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, "index.html")):
              sys.exit("public/index.html missing")
          n = total = 0; big = []
          for d, _, fs in os.walk(root):
              for f in fs:
                  p = os.path.join(d, f); s = os.path.getsize(p)
                  n += 1; total += s
                  if s > 25 * 1024 * 1024: big.append(f"{p} ({s/2**20:.1f} MiB)")
          print(f"{n} files, {total/1e6:.1f} MB")
          if n > 20000: sys.exit(f"{n} files > 20,000 (CF Pages Free)")
          if big: sys.exit("files over 25 MiB: " + ", ".join(big))
          if total > 1_000_000_000: sys.exit("over GitHub Pages 1 GB published-site limit")
          PY
      - if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        id: pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6    # outputs base_path (e.g. /REPO) if you need it
      - if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: public/
          # include-hidden-files: true      # v5 input; needed for .well-known/ etc.
      - if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7     # separate copy for the Cloudflare job
        with:
          name: site
          path: public/
          retention-days: 3
          include-hidden-files: true

  deploy-gh-pages:
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pages: write        # to deploy to Pages
      id-token: write     # OIDC token the Pages API validates
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    concurrency:
      group: pages
      cancel-in-progress: false            # never kill an in-flight Pages deploy
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

  deploy-cloudflare:
    needs: build
    # vars.* allowed here; secrets.* is NOT allowed in if: -> second gate below via env
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && vars.CF_PAGES_PROJECT != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      deployments: write                   # only needed because gitHubToken is passed
    concurrency:
      group: cloudflare-pages
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      HAS_CF: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN != '' && secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID != '' }}
    steps:
      - if: env.HAS_CF != 'true'
        run: echo "::notice::Cloudflare secrets not set - skipping Cloudflare deploy"
      - if: env.HAS_CF == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7          # brings functions/ (+ package.json if Functions use npm deps)
      - if: env.HAS_CF == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: site
          path: public
      - if: env.HAS_CF == 'true'
        id: cf
        uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4   # avoid v4.1.0/v4.1.1 (broken)
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          # run from repo root so ./functions (next to ./public) is compiled + uploaded
          command: pages deploy public --project-name=${{ vars.CF_PAGES_PROJECT }} --branch=main --commit-hash=${{ github.sha }}
          gitHubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - if: env.HAS_CF == 'true'
        run: echo "Cloudflare deployment ${{ steps.cf.outputs.deployment-url }}"

# =====================================================================
# 2) .github/workflows/backup.yml  - weekly release w/ zip, keep newest 12
# =====================================================================
name: Weekly backup
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 7 * * 1'      # Mondays 07:23 UTC (off the top of the hour = fewer delays)
      # timezone: "America/Los_Angeles"   # optional IANA key, newly documented
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write             # create releases/tags, delete old ones

concurrency:
  group: backup
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  backup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      KEEP: 12
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Zip the repo at HEAD (content/, media, templates, build code)
        run: |
          STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
          echo "TAG=backup-$STAMP" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          git archive --format=zip --prefix=site/ -o "site-backup-$STAMP.zip" HEAD
          sha256sum "site-backup-$STAMP.zip" > "site-backup-$STAMP.zip.sha256"
          ls -lh site-backup-*          # each asset must be < 2 GiB
      - name: Create release
        run: |
          gh release create "$TAG" site-backup-*.zip site-backup-*.zip.sha256 \
            --title "Backup $TAG" \
            --notes "Automated snapshot of $GITHUB_SHA" \
            --target "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --latest=false
      - name: Prune to newest $KEEP backups
        run: |
          gh release list --limit 200 --exclude-drafts --json tagName,createdAt \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.tagName | startswith("backup-"))] | sort_by(.createdAt) | reverse | .['"$KEEP"':] | .[].tagName' |
          while read -r t; do
            [ -n "$t" ] || continue
            echo "Deleting $t"
            gh release delete "$t" --cleanup-tag --yes
          done

# =====================================================================
# 3) .github/workflows/restore.yml  - restore content/ from a named release
# =====================================================================
name: Restore content from backup
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Backup release tag, e.g. backup-20261026-072301'
        required: true
        type: string
      paths:
        description: 'Space-separated folders to restore'
        required: false
        default: 'content'
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write             # push the restore commit
  actions: write              # gh workflow run (GITHUB_TOKEN push won't fire on: push)

concurrency:
  group: content-write
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  restore:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}              # pass inputs via env, never inline in run: (injection)
      RESTORE_PATHS: ${{ inputs.paths }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Validate tag
        run: |
          [[ "$TAG" =~ ^backup-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]] || { echo "bad tag: $TAG"; exit 1; }
          gh release view "$TAG" > /dev/null
      - name: Download + verify + unzip
        run: |
          D="$RUNNER_TEMP/restore"; mkdir -p "$D"
          gh release download "$TAG" --pattern 'site-backup-*' --dir "$D"
          (cd "$D" && sha256sum -c site-backup-*.zip.sha256)
          unzip -q "$D"/site-backup-*.zip -d "$D/x"
      - name: Replace folders
        run: |
          for p in $RESTORE_PATHS; do
            [[ "$p" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ && "$p" != *..* ]] || { echo "bad path: $p"; exit 1; }
            src="$RUNNER_TEMP/restore/x/site/$p"
            [ -d "$src" ] || { echo "$p not in backup"; exit 1; }
            mkdir -p "$p"
            rsync -a --delete "$src/" "$p/"
          done
          git status --short
      - name: Commit + push
        run: |
          git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A -- $RESTORE_PATHS
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo "Nothing changed"; exit 0; fi
          git commit -m "Restore $RESTORE_PATHS from $TAG"
          git push
          echo "PUSHED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Kick build/deploy (workflow_dispatch is exempt from the GITHUB_TOKEN rule)
        if: env.PUSHED == '1'
        run: gh workflow run site.yml --ref "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"

# =====================================================================
# 4) Cloudflare Web Analytics - production-only beacon (site NOT proxied)
# =====================================================================
# Option A (Cloudflare Pages): Workers & Pages > project > Metrics > Web Analytics > Enable
#   -> auto-injected on next deployment; GH Pages preview never gets it.
#   (Unverified whether the toggle is offered for Direct Upload projects.)
# Option B (manual; works anywhere): Web Analytics > Add a site > hostname > copy token.
#   Standard snippet before </body>:
#   <script defer src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js"
#           data-cf-beacon='{"token": "YOUR_SITE_TOKEN"}'></script>
#   One artifact is shared by GH Pages + CF, so load it only on the prod host,
#   using an external file (no inline script, CSP-friendly) /js/analytics.js:
#     if (location.hostname === 'www.example.com') {
#       var s = document.createElement('script'); s.defer = true;
#       s.src = 'https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js?token=YOUR_SITE_TOKEN'; // documented tag-manager form
#       document.head.appendChild(s);
#     }
# public/_headers (Cloudflare only; GitHub Pages ignores it):
# /*
#   Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com; connect-src 'self' https://cloudflareinsights.com; img-src 'self' data:
# (Add any Instagram-embed origins here too if widgets are added - not researched in this brief.)

# =====================================================================
# 5) If you use Cloudflare Git integration instead of wrangler (not recommended here)
# =====================================================================
# Build command:    pip install -r requirements.txt && python build.py
# Output directory: public
# Env var:          PYTHON_VERSION=3.13   (or commit .python-version)
# functions/ stays at repo root (NOT inside public/). 20-min build timeout; pip is not build-cached.
gotchas: A restore commit pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN will not start the on: push build, so the restore workflow has to dispatch the build itself (gh workflow run, which needs actions: write) or call it as a reusable workflow. A PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN won't run checks either.
If main has branch protection that requires PRs or reviews, the restore job's direct `git push` with GITHUB_TOKEN will be rejected. Use a bypass or an App token, or open a PR and merge it by hand.
Secrets are not allowed in `jobs.<id>.if` or `steps.if`. Gate on `vars.*` at job level and on a job-level env var derived from secrets at step level, as in the snippet.

GitHub Pages project sites are served under /REPO/ unless you use a custom domain, while Cloudflare serves at /. One shared artifact only works if the templates use relative URLs. Otherwise build twice (configure-pages exposes `base_path`) or give the preview a custom domain.
GitHub Pages ignores functions/, _headers and _redirects. The two /api/* Functions only work on Cloudflare, so the preview needs a graceful fallback.
upload-pages-artifact v4+ drops dotfiles (.well-known/, .nojekyll) by default. v5 has `include-hidden-files: true`, and upload-artifact also defaults include-hidden-files to false.
A Cloudflare Direct Upload project (wrangler) can never be converted to Git integration. Pick the mode before creating the project.

Cloudflare's docs never say requirements.txt is auto-installed, and pip isn't in the Pages build cache. If you use Git integration, put the pip install in the build command. opencv/numpy wheel installs count toward the 20-minute build timeout.
v1 Cloudflare build-image projects were force-moved to v3 on Sep 15 2026, so Python defaults to 3.13.3. v2 projects move on Feb 23 2027. Pin PYTHON_VERSION or commit .python-version.
Cloudflare Free has a 20,000-file limit and a 25 MiB per-file limit. Image-pipeline outputs (AVIF/WebP size ladders) can multiply the file count fast, which is why the validation step enforces both.

On GitHub Free, Pages needs a public repo, and then every backup release zip is public too. Keep secrets and drafts out of the repo. With Pro (Student Pack), a private repo works, but the Pages site itself is still public.
If immutable releases is turned on, a deleted backup tag name can't be reused, so tags must be unique timestamps. Attach assets at creation, or create as a draft, attach, then publish.

Scheduled workflows run only on the default branch, can be delayed (worst at the top of the hour), and auto-disable after 60 days without repo activity in public repos. The docs say nothing about private repos.
wrangler-action v4.1.0 and v4.1.1 are broken. Use @v4 or v4.1.2+. v4 installs Wrangler v4 by default.

The docs.github.com Pages examples still pin configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v4 and deploy-pages@v4. The release pages show v6, v5 and v5 as Latest, and the starter workflow already uses deploy-pages@v5. Release pages show no year; the latest dates are inferred to be 2026.
Pages CMS makes one commit per save. Collapse bursts with build-job concurrency (cancel-in-progress: true), but keep cancel-in-progress: false on the Pages and Cloudflare deploy jobs.
Web Analytics allows 10 non-proxied sites (soft limit), and ad blockers can block the beacon. The data-cf-beacon token is public by design and is not a secret.
recommendation:
Build once in GitHub Actions and deploy that same output to both GitHub Pages (preview) and Cloudflare Pages (production, via wrangler Direct Upload). Skip Cloudflare's Git integration because:
- Pip caching works in Actions; Cloudflare's build cache doesn't cover pip.
- Nothing depends on the undocumented requirements.txt auto-install, the 20-minute Cloudflare build limit, or the build-image v1/v2-to-v3 moves.
- Preview and production are byte-identical.
- `wrangler pages deploy public` run from the repo root picks up `functions/api/*` automatically.

Setup:
1. Create the Cloudflare project with `wrangler pages project create` (Direct Upload is permanent).
2. Add the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID secrets and a CF_PAGES_PROJECT repo variable.
3. Switch the GitHub Pages source with `gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/pages -f build_type=workflow` (POST if Pages isn't enabled yet).

Pin these versions: checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5, upload-artifact@v7, download-artifact@v8, wrangler-action@v4.

Pages CMS commits trigger the build on their own, because they're made with its App installation token or the user's token, not GITHUB_TOKEN.

Backups:
- A weekly scheduled job runs `git archive` and publishes it as a GitHub Release (assets under 2 GiB, no total cap), keeping the newest 12 with `gh release delete --cleanup-tag`.
- Releases beat artifacts here: artifacts expire after at most 90 days (public) or 400 (private).
- The restore job (workflow_dispatch) rsyncs content/ back from the chosen tag, commits, and then has to dispatch the build itself, since a GITHUB_TOKEN push won't trigger it.

Hosting:
- Repo visibility: Pages from a private repo needs Pro, which the Student Pack covers. Otherwise keep the repo public and treat backups as public.
- For bad Cloudflare deploys, use the dashboard "Rollback to this deployment" first; git restores are for content mistakes.

Analytics: try the Cloudflare Pages Web Analytics toggle first, since it is production-only with no code. If it isn't offered for a Direct Upload project, use the hostname-guarded beacon in an external JS file, and allow static.cloudflareinsights.com and cloudflareinsights.com in the `_headers` CSP. Instagram widgets would need their own CSP additions; they weren't researched here.

summary:
Sources: the whole Pages CMS documentation (its Markdown source in hunvreus/pagescms-website, spot-checked against the live pagescms.org pages) and the app's source at v2.1.8 (commit 6f4e860). pages-cms/pages-cms now redirects to hunvreus/pagescms. v2.1.8 (2026-06-08) is the latest release, and app.pagescms.org/api/app/version also reports 2.1.8. Pages CMS fits the job: the manager is invited by email, has no access to .pages.yml or collaborator settings, and every field is validated against your schema on screen and again on the server. There are seven traps for a JSON-driven site, and most are not in the docs:
(1) Each save rewrites the whole file from the schema. Keys you did not declare are deleted (settings.content.merge defaults to false). Even with merge on, lists are replaced whole and the merge has open bugs.
(2) Empty values ("", null, [], {}) are removed from the JSON, the file is rewritten with 2-space indentation and no final newline, and keys follow the field order in .pages.yml.
(3) A JSON collection must set a `filename` ending in .json, or its entries silently disappear (open bug #413).
(4) The object form of `list` (with min/max) breaks the editor when used at the top level of a single file (bug #399). Use `list: true` there, or put the list inside an object field.
(5) The hosted app runs on Vercel, so uploads over about 3.3 MB fail with error 413: the 4.5 MB request limit applies after base64 encoding.
(6) Collaborators can delete any file in the media folders and can create or switch branches.
(7) The server starting an action does not check the request against .pages.yml. Any CMS user can start any workflow that accepts a `payload` input, on any branch.
There is no preview and no in-app undo. The history panel shows the last three commits as links to GitHub.
The example .pages.yml below passes Pages CMS's own config validator (checked by running lib/config-schema.ts locally against it). Your original request mentioned Instagram widgets. This brief only covers Pages CMS, so the example adds an Instagram handle field and a featured-post-URL list, which let the manager control an Instagram section. How to build the embed or widget itself was not researched here.

findings.detail: pages-cms/pages-cms redirects to hunvreus/pagescms. Latest release 2.1.8 (2026-06-08). https://app.pagescms.org/api/app/version returns {"latest":"2.1.8"}. Docs are built from hunvreus/pagescms-website/docs/*.md. Branch overhaul/tanstack-start is 100 commits ahead of main (SQLite, Google sign-in, local drafts; last commit 2026-10-16) and not merged. Hosted behaviour may change when it lands.

name* (letters, digits, - and _ only), label (string, or false to hide), type* OR component (exactly one), required, pattern, hidden, readonly (passed down to nested object/block/list fields), description (help text under the field), options (per-type settings). `default` is not in the docs table, but the config schema accepts it (any value) and per-field pages use it (boolean `default: true`; date/uuid `default: ""` keeps the field blank). Field objects are strict: a key such as top-level `minlength` gets the warning "isn't valid and will be ignored". Per-type settings go under `options:`.

Documented for string and text only (source shows rich-text checks it too). Either `pattern: "^[a-z0-9-]+$"` or `pattern: { regex: "...", message: "..." }`. Default error messages: "Invalid format" (string form) and "Invalid pattern format" (object form without message).

findings.topic: Optional fields with pattern/minlength reject blanks
findings.detail: String fields default to "", and zod runs regex and min checks on "". An optional field with a pattern or minlength therefore fails validation when left blank. Confirmed with zod 3.25.76. Write patterns as "^$|<regex>" and avoid minlength on optional fields.

`list: true`, or the object form `list: { min, max, collapsible }`. collapsible is true, false, or { collapsed: bool, summary: "{title} ({index})" }; tokens are {index}, {fields.x} and {x}. Adding `required: true` to a list means at least one item. The config validator (lib/config-schema.ts) requires `collapsible` whenever the object form is used: `list: {min: 1, max: 6}` alone gives a "Required" error (reproduced). That error only shows in the in-app config editor, so add `collapsible: false` anyway.

findings.topic: string / text / number / boolean / code / uuid options
findings.detail: string and text: options.minlength, options.maxlength. number: options.min, options.max (values are coerced to numbers; a blank is saved as "" and then removed). boolean: no options, defaults to false. code: options.format (yaml, js, json, html, markdown, mdx…). uuid: options.editable, options.generate; generated automatically unless `default` is set. Source shows rich-text also honours minlength/maxlength (not in docs).

options.values (required): a list of strings, or [{name, label}], which stores `name` and shows `label` (the source also accepts `value`). Also options.multiple (bool), min, max (only with multiple), placeholder. There is no creatable or free-text option; anything outside values fails on save with "Invalid option". For dynamic options the docs point to `reference`.

findings.topic: image field options and stored value
findings.detail: options: media (named media source), path (default browsing folder), multiple (true or { max: N }), extensions, categories ([image]), unique, rename (false|true|safe|random). Source: on write, the media `input` prefix is swapped for `output` (src/assets/uploads/a.jpg → "/assets/uploads/a.jpg"). multiple stores an array of strings. Without options.media the first media source is used. The built-in image category is jpg, jpeg, apng, png, gif, svg, ico, avif, bmp, tif, tiff, webp; HEIC is not included.

options: time (true adds a time picker), format (date-fns tokens, e.g. yyyy-MM-dd), min, max, step. New dates default to today (date-time fields to now) unless `default: ""`. Source: values are stored as formatted strings. min/max are parsed as yyyy-MM-dd (or yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm). An existing value that doesn't parse with `format` is read as "" and then dropped on save. Timezone handling of date-times is a known issue (#247, open PR #410).

object: nested `fields` with no options of its own. `required` applies to the object itself, and child `required` rules only kick in once the object has content. block: `blocks` plus `blockKey` (default `_block`). A block cannot be a list itself; nest a list inside it. reference: options collection, multiple, min, max, search, value/label templates ({path}, {name}, {primary}, {fields.x}). An open issue (#311) says single-file content cannot be referenced.

Single file with `fields`; format is inferred from a .json extension when fields exist, but setting it explicitly is safer. Object fields show as grouped inputs. Object lists show as repeatable items with add, remove and drag-to-reorder, and can be collapsed with a summary line. `list: true` on the content entry makes the whole file a top-level array. The docs say "the documented form is `list: true`". The object form at the top level shows one blank item instead of the data (#399; fix PR #455 still open).

findings.topic: Undeclared keys are deleted on save (critical)
findings.detail: settings.content.merge: false is the default: "Rewrite the file from the configured schema only. Anything outside the submitted editor output is removed." With `merge: true`, the submitted fields are merged into the existing file and keys outside the schema are kept.

Saving runs zod (which strips unknown keys) and only walks declared fields. Merge uses lodash mergeWith, where arrays replace the old arrays whole, so undeclared keys inside list items are always lost. Merge is skipped completely for `list: true` files and for new files. Open bugs: a cleared optional object comes back after save (#387), and a field sometimes reverts (#431).

findings.topic: JSON rewriting: empty-value removal and formatting (source)
findings.detail: Output is JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2): 2-space indent, no final newline. sanitizeObject deletes keys whose value is null, "", [] or {}, and drops empty list items. false and 0 are kept. Key order follows the field order in .pages.yml (with merge: the existing order, then new keys). The site code must handle missing keys.

If `filename` is left out, normalizeConfig defaults it to "{year}-{month}-{day}-{primary}.md", so the extension becomes md. A format: json collection then lists zero entries and new saves fail the extension check. Open issue #413. Set e.g. `filename: "{fields.date}-{fields.title}.json"`. Filename tokens: {primary}/{slug}, {year} {month} {day} {hour} {minute} {second}, and {fields.x} / {x} (values are slugified).

name*, label, type* (collection|file|group), path*, fields, filename, exclude, format (yaml-frontmatter, json-frontmatter, toml-frontmatter, yaml, json, toml, datagrid, code, raw), delimiters, subfolders, list, view (fields, primary, sort, search, default.{search,sort,order}, layout list|tree, node), operations, commit, actions, items (for groups). Operation defaults: collection create/rename/delete = true/true/true; file = true/false/TRUE. Lock single files with operations.delete: false. Leaving out `fields` gives a raw-text editor.

Can be a string (`media: media` means input media, output /media), one object, or an array of named sources. Keys: name (required in an array), label, input* (repo path, no leading or trailing slash), output* (public prefix written into content), extensions, categories (image, document, video, audio, compressed, code, font, spreadsheet), rename (false = keep name (default), true/safe = slugify, random), commit (templates, identity), actions. Field-level options override media defaults. The source shows that if both extensions and categories are set, extensions wins. There is no upload-size option.

Pages CMS itself sets no size limit. The browser base64-encodes each upload and sends it as JSON to the app's API route, and Vercel caps request bodies at 4.5 MB, so files over about 3.3 MB fail with 413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. Open issue #393, closed #284 (the maintainer says it's a Vercel limit: self-host elsewhere), open PRs #408 (chunked uploads) and #425 (resize in the browser). Ordinary phone photos can hit this.

Media deletes and renames have no `operations` check. Any user with repo access, collaborators included, can delete or rename any file under a media source's `input` folder. They cannot touch paths outside it. Keep logos and layout images outside the media input folders.

Invited by email; meant for people without a GitHub account. They can open the repos they were invited to and edit content and media; create/rename/delete still follow content.operations. They cannot manage .pages.yml, collaborators, or the cache. Writes use the GitHub App installation token. By default commits carry the app's identity; `commit.identity: user` adds the collaborator's name and email. Collaborators are stored in the Pages CMS database, not in .pages.yml. Source: the invite link expires after 24 h (env COLLABORATOR_INVITE_LINK_EXPIRES_IN, undocumented). Sign-in uses a 6-digit emailed code that is valid for 5 minutes.

Docs: `Run again` is for GitHub users only; collaborators can only cancel their own active runs. Source: repo-level actions appear in the sidebar Actions group for every user, so collaborators can trigger them. The Actions history page and the links to GitHub run pages are for GitHub users only. Collaborators see run status without links.

findings.topic: Collaborators can create and switch branches
findings.detail: The create-branch API and the branch switcher do not require a GitHub identity, so a collaborator can edit on a branch that never deploys. There is no PR or draft step: saves commit straight to the open branch.

Account: Email addresses (read). Repository: Administration (read/write), Actions (read/write), Checks (read), Commit statuses (read), Contents (read/write), Metadata (read). Events: Installation target, Repository, Push, Delete, Check run, Check suite, Status, Workflow run. Turn off user-to-server token expiration. When self-hosting, the documented setup command is `npm run setup:github-app`. On the hosted app, install it on the site repo only.

name*, label*, workflow* (file in .github/workflows), ref (leave it out, or set `current`, to use the branch open in the CMS), scope (collection actions only: collection|entry, and required there; not allowed on file actions), cancelable (default true), confirm (dialog by default; false skips it; or { title, message, button }), fields (name, label, type text|textarea|select|checkbox|number, required, default, options [{label, value}] which select requires). If fields are set, the dialog shows even with confirm: false. The repo must have GitHub Actions enabled, and the workflow must declare `workflow_dispatch` with a string input named `payload`.

Source: after a click, a toast goes "Starting \"X\"…" → "Waiting for GitHub to start \"X\"…" → "\"X\" is running." → "succeeded / failed / was cancelled / timed out / was skipped". It polls every 4 s, keeps tracking for up to 12 h (in sessionStorage), and shows a Cancel button when allowed. Each action button also has a dropdown of recent runs with a spinner, check or X icon, relative time and "by <name>". Status comes from workflow_run webhooks and API lookups.

One JSON string in inputs.payload: { source: "pages-cms", action: {name, label[, cancelable]}, repository: {owner, repo, ref, workflowRef, sha}, triggeredAt, triggeredBy: {userId, name, email, githubUsername, image}, context: {type, name, path, data}, inputs: {...} }. Reruns add triggerType: "rerun" and rerunOfActionRunId. Source: context.type is repo, collection, entry, file or media; root actions send "repo".

POST /api/[owner]/[repo]/[branch]/actions takes action.workflow and action.ref from the request body and never checks them against .pages.yml. Any CMS user with repo access, collaborators included, could start any workflow that declares a `payload` input, on any branch. Field values are also passed through without checking them against the select options. Guard every such workflow: check the branch, allow-list inputs, and never put payload strings directly into `run:` scripts.

settings: hide (hides the Configuration page), content.merge, commit.templates (defaults: "Create {path} (via Pages CMS)", "Update …", "Delete …", "Rename {oldPath} to {newPath} (via Pages CMS)"), commit.identity app (default) | user. Per-entry and per-media overrides via content[].commit and media[].commit. Tokens: {action} {path} {filename} {name} {owner} {repo} {branch} {user} {userName} {userEmail} {oldPath} {newPath} {oldFilename} {newFilename}.

Source: userName and userEmail come from the committer object, which only exists when identity resolves to `user`. With the default `app` they are empty strings, while {user} (email, then name, then id) still works. The docs' advice to prefer {userName}/{userEmail} only holds with identity: user.

Source: the entry editor's history block or dropdown shows the last 3 commits (author, relative time), each linking to github.com, plus a "See all changes" / "View on GitHub" link. There is no in-app revert or restore, so undo means a git revert by a developer. On a private repo, collaborators without GitHub access cannot open those links. There is no preview feature in 2.1.8: branch feature/preview ("WIP Preview", 2026-06-23), issue #190 and PR #336 are all still open.

GitHub is the source of truth; PostgreSQL is a read cache. .pages.yml is cached per owner/repo/branch. Defaults: CONFIG_CHECK_MIN 5, CACHE_CHECK_MIN 5, FILE_TTL_MIN 1440, PERMISSIONS_TTL_MIN 60. Push webhooks update the cache. Issue #431 reports config edits made outside the CMS sometimes not showing up.

Collections over ~1,000 files time out on the hosted app (#310). Directories with large total content hit a GraphQL Blob.text limit (#423). Images in Git LFS are broken (#407, PR #451). In private repos, a rich-text image can be saved as a blob: URL when its preview fails (#438). GitHub user tokens on the hosted app expire after 8 h and show up as a misleading "no permission" error (#402); collaborators are not affected. A number stored in a field declared as string fails with "Expected string, received number" (#431). Booleans use z.coerce, so the string "false" becomes true. No rate-limit documentation was found.

options.format markdown (default) or html; switcher (Editor/Source toggle, default true); media (false disables image insertion); path, extensions, categories, rename. The Source mode lets editors type raw markdown or HTML. To protect layout, use text with maxlength, or rich-text with switcher: false and media: false.

# ===================== .github/workflows/pages-cms-publish.yml =====================
name: "Pages CMS: Publish site"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      payload:                         # Pages CMS sends ONE JSON string here
        description: Pages CMS payload as JSON
        required: true
        type: string
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: publish-site
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  publish:
    # Pages CMS doesn't check the workflow/ref against .pages.yml, so guard here.
    if: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.payload).source == 'pages-cms' && fromJSON(inputs.payload).repository.ref == 'main' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
      - name: Log who triggered it (payload goes in through env, never inlined into the script)
        env:
          PAYLOAD: ${{ inputs.payload }}
        run: echo "$PAYLOAD" | jq '{action: .action.name, by: .triggeredBy.name, ref: .repository.ref}'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run validate:content  # JSON Schema check of src/_data/**/*.json; fails before anything ships
      - run: npm run build
      # - name: Deploy
      #   env: { DEPLOY_HOOK: "${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOOK_URL }}" }
      #   run: curl -fsS -X POST "$DEPLOY_HOOK"

# ===================== .github/workflows/pages-cms-check.yml =====================
name: "Pages CMS: Check site"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      payload:
        description: Pages CMS payload as JSON
        required: true
        type: string
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.payload).repository.ref }}   # the branch open in the CMS
      - name: Read options (allow-listed; Pages CMS does not check select values)
        id: opts
        env:
          PAYLOAD: ${{ inputs.payload }}
        run: |
          SCOPE=$(echo "$PAYLOAD" | jq -r '.inputs.scope // "content"')
          case "$SCOPE" in content|links) ;; *) SCOPE=content ;; esac
          echo "scope=$SCOPE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run validate:content
      - if: steps.opts.outputs.scope == 'links'
        run: npm run build && npm run check:links
