gotchas: Each save rewrites the file from the schema: keys you did not declare are deleted (merge defaults to false). Even with `settings.content.merge: true`, lists are replaced whole (extra keys inside list items are still lost), merge is skipped for `list: true` files, and there are open merge bugs (#387 a cleared object comes back, #431 a field reverts). Treat .pages.yml as the full contract for every CMS-managed JSON file.

Blank values are removed from the JSON ("", null, [], {}), so the site must use defaults for missing keys such as `special` or `open`. The JSON is rewritten with 2-space indentation, no final newline, and keys in field order. Run every CMS-managed file through the CMS once before go-live so later diffs stay clean.
A JSON collection must set `filename` ending in `.json`. The default template ends in .md and the entries silently disappear (open issue #413).

Never use the object form of `list` ({min, max, collapsible}) at the top level of a single file. The editor shows a blank item instead of the data (#399; fix PR #455 still open). Use `list: true` there, or put the list inside an object field as in the example.

The object form of `list` must include `collapsible` (e.g. `collapsible: false`), or the in-app config editor shows a 'Required' error. Per-type settings such as minlength must sit under `options:`; at the top level they are ignored with a warning.
An optional string or text field with a `pattern` or `minlength` rejects a blank value. Write patterns as "^$|..." and use minlength only on required fields.

Date values already in the JSON must match `options.format`. Values that don't match are read as blank and deleted on the next save. Date min/max are written as yyyy-MM-dd. Without `default: ""`, new date fields start at today.

Type mismatches block saving: a number in a field declared `string` fails with 'Expected string, received number' (#431). Booleans use z.coerce, so the string "false" becomes true. Clean existing JSON types before switching on the CMS.

Hosted app.pagescms.org runs on Vercel, so uploads over about 3.3 MB fail with error 413 (4.5 MB body limit after base64; #393 open, PRs #408/#425 open). Tell the manager to resize photos, or self-host on a non-Vercel host. HEIC is not in the image category.
Collaborators can delete or rename any file under a media `input` folder (media has no `operations` lock). Keep logos and layout images outside those folders.
Single files default to `delete: true`. Set `operations: { delete: false }` on the settings file, and `rename: false` (and `delete: false` if wanted) on collections.

Collaborators can create and switch branches, and saves go straight to whatever branch is open. Edits on a non-main branch never deploy. Show the manager the branch picker and keep the guard on `repository.ref` in the workflows.

The server that starts actions does not check the request against .pages.yml. Any CMS user can start any workflow with a `payload` input, on any branch, with any input values. Add `payload` only to safe workflows, check source/ref, allow-list inputs, and pass the payload through `env` + jq, never `${{ }}` inside `run:`.
Commit tokens {userName}/{userEmail} are empty unless `commit.identity: user`. With the default `app` identity, use {user}.

There is no in-app undo or preview in 2.1.8. History shows the last 3 commits as GitHub links, which collaborators can't open on a private repo. Rollback means a developer runs git revert. Preview is only a WIP branch (#190, #336).
Collaborator invite links expire after 24 h (env COLLABORATOR_INVITE_LINK_EXPIRES_IN, undocumented), and the emailed sign-in code is valid for 5 minutes. Re-invite if she misses the window.
The hosted GitHub App needs Administration read/write, Actions read/write and Contents read/write. Install it on the single site repo only, not 'All repositories'.
GitHub user sessions on the hosted app expire after 8 h and show up as 'You do not have permission' (#402). Sign out and back in. Email collaborators are not affected.
Edits to .pages.yml made directly on GitHub can take up to about 5 min (CONFIG_CHECK_MIN) or a webhook to appear. Intermittent staleness is reported in #431.
In private repos, rich-text image inserts can be saved as blob: URLs (#438), and Git LFS media is broken (#407). Use image fields, not rich-text images, and don't store media in LFS.
A large rewrite (overhaul/tanstack-start, 100 commits ahead, active through 2026-10-16) has not been merged. Hosted behaviour could change when it ships, so re-test the config after major releases.
recommendation:
Use hosted Pages CMS (app.pagescms.org, v2.1.8), installed on the single site repo only. Invite the marketing manager as an email collaborator, so she never touches .pages.yml, collaborators or GitHub. To make sure she can't break the layout:
(a) Keep anything that controls layout (section order, CSS classes, nav, feature flags, layout images) in JSON files and folders that are NOT listed in .pages.yml.
(b) Leave settings.content.merge off and declare every key the site reads in the schema. Write site code that handles missing keys, because blank values are removed on save.
(c) Prefer string/text fields with maxlength and patterns, and select fields with fixed values, over rich-text. If you do use rich-text, set switcher: false and media: false.
(d) Lock structure with operations (delete: false on the settings file, rename: false on events) and fixed-length lists (min/max 7 for weekly hours, inside an object field, never at the file root).
(e) Use a dedicated uploads folder with extensions limited to jpg/jpeg/png/webp. Tell her to keep photos under 3 MB, or self-host off Vercel if that's too tight.
(f) Add a CI step that checks every content JSON against a JSON Schema before every deploy, so a bad edit fails the build instead of reaching the live site.
(g) Include the two workflows above, each guarded on source, branch and allowed inputs.
Before go-live, clean the existing JSON (date formats, number vs string types) and save each file once through the CMS so later diffs only show content changes. Tell the client plainly that there is no preview or undo button: rollback is a git revert by you. For the Instagram widget idea, the example gives the manager a handle field and a validated featured-post-URL list. How to render the widget or embed still needs its own research.
